answer: One concrete mechanism: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because quill only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, lagoon is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any sable approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
